task.text: `AppConfig.get()` is supposed to give every thread the same object. It does not.

Three things break the guarantee: threads can race through lazy creation, reflection can call the private constructor, and deserialization quietly makes a new instance. Fix `AppConfig` so that exactly one instance exists, however it is reached.

items: Keep the constructor calling `Probe.constructed()` once per instance. `Probe.java` is a read-only test seam.
Lazy initialization is fine, an `enum` or holder class is welcome, but a plain unsynchronized check is not.

checks.title: Eight racing threads share one instance
Reflection cannot build a second instance

hints.text: There are three separate doors to a second instance: concurrent first calls, the reflection API, and Java serialization. Each needs its own answer. The class loader already makes one of them safe for free.

Put the instance in a private nested `Holder` class so the JVM initializes it once, on first use. Make the constructor refuse a second call, and give the class a `readResolve` that returns the shared instance.
